vision.title: Where teachers learn, share and lead
vision.sub: HunarNet is an open, continuous professional learning space for vocational and experiential-education teachers — built on conversation before content, and contribution before consumption.
vision.card_learn_body: Understand NEP 2020 and vocational pedagogy through study circles rooted in real classroom realities, not lectures.
vision.card_share_body: Share what works — a lesson, a tool, a project, a reflection — and learn from what's working in classrooms across India.
vision.card_lead_body: Turn contribution into recognition, and recognition into peer leadership through the Fellowship pathway.

pillars.title: Community pillars
pillars.sub: Everything in HunarNet grows from three ongoing spaces of exchange.

items.name: NEP Study Circles
items.body: Peer-led discussions that unpack NEP 2020 — vocational integration, pedagogy, resource readiness, assessment and timetable alignment — always rooted in what's actually happening in schools.

items.name: Charcha
items.h: A safe space to discuss what is actually happening in schools.
items.body: Open forums for classroom challenges, school leadership constraints and resource limitations — framed as solution-building conversations, never complaint forums.

items.name: Guest Knowledge Exchange
items.h: Learn with experts, practitioners and institutions.
items.body: Two-way sessions with experts and practitioners — built for questioning and contextual adaptation, not one-directional lectures.

loop.title: From contribution to leadership
loop.sub: This loop — not a linear course — is what makes HunarNet a living community. Click a stage to see how it works.

stages.name: Learn
stages.detail: Understand NEP and vocational pedagogy through study circles and guest sessions.

stages.name: Practice
stages.detail: Apply ideas in your own classroom, adapted to your students and resources.

stages.name: Share
stages.detail: Share what happened — the attempt, the outcome, the lesson learned.

stages.name: Recognition
stages.detail: Get recognised through community shout-outs and the Teacher Practice Spotlight.

stages.name: Lead
stages.detail: Take on visible leadership — lead a session, a discussion, a theme.

stages.name: Mentor
stages.detail: Mentor five other teachers as a HunarNet Fellow.

stages.name: Help Others
stages.detail: Your mentees start their own loop — and the community compounds.

faqs.title: Frequently asked questions
faqs.sub: Everything you need to know before joining the community.

items.a: Any teacher working with vocational, experiential or NEP-aligned education. The community begins with a seed group from Kaushal Bodh, Atal Tinkering Labs and multi-sector vocational programs, and opens up to more teachers over time.

items.q: How much time does it take?
items.a: As much or as little as fits your schedule. There are live sessions roughly once or twice a month, plus ongoing discussion you can dip into whenever you like — there's no minimum attendance requirement.
Yes. HunarNet is a free professional-learning community facilitated by Lend A Hand India — there is no membership fee.
Charcha is our peer discussion space for real classroom and school-level challenges. It's built for solution-building conversations, not complaint forums.

items.q: How do I become a Fellow?
items.a: Fellowship is optional. Fellows are selected through peer nominations, contribution score and community polls, and go on to mentor five other teachers and lead thematic discussions.

items.q: Do I need any special qualification or tech skill?
items.a: No. All you need is classroom experience and a willingness to share, learn and support fellow teachers.
